timecoded_text_to_speech.text: So a walk in their shoes is a six piece portfolio.
All these quilted pieces are more or less portraits of people, but I didn't want it to just
be their faces. I wanted to be their stories. I wanted to kind of be able to take the audience
and have them literally walk in the shoes of these individuals. I interviewed every single
person and then took those various aspects of that interview that really stuck out to
me and sort of created a visual narrative of their story and their outlook on life.
To create all of the pieces, I start with a digital sort of mock-up, a very rough,
on an iPad and using an Apple Pencil, the Procreate app, and then from there I go on to post-realization
softwares and then all of that gets put into the Cricket Design Space software, which
computerizes those images to cut them out of fabric. And then from there it gets cut
out into the fabric pieces itself. That's where I pick all the colors, the patterns,
how things are going to overlay. And then those pieces are kind of put together like
a puzzle to create individual components and they're attached a little bit with glue
before they're finally quilted on the background, component after component, and then sort
of like final touches are added.
NCSSM has played a really big role in helping not just get me sort of from a conceptual
standpoint where I need to be to get these pieces the best that they can be, but they've
also been really, really amazing at helping me promote my artwork.
Specifically, I've been involved with the Advanced 3 Art Program and Miss Alter has been
really amazing at helping push those ideas, helping me get social media started, helping
me promote my artwork. I've had access to FabLab sewing machines and boarding machines.
I've had access to photography equipment to help film the process. I've had access to
teachers who helped me write about these pieces and also just regular materials from fabric
to thread and whatnot. And also the space, this wonderful art space that is collaborative
with other students.

youtube_description:
Mac Barnes ’22 recently won the Gold Medal Portfolio Award for Art in the 2022 Scholastic Art & Writing Awards national competition for his 6-piece portfolio “A Walk in Their Shoes.” Each quilt was inspired by interviews with the subject of their focus.

Barnes stitched these together using the quilted appliqué technique, a means of sewing pieces directly on top of the quilt rather than together. 

See more of his work at https://sites.google.com/view/macbarnes.

NCSSM, a publicly funded high school in North Carolina, provides exciting, high-level STEM learning opportunities. If you appreciate this video, please consider making a tax-deductible donation to the NCSSM Foundation. Thank you!  https://www.ncssm.edu/donate
